faqs.q: What are the Subclass 189, 190 and 491 visas?

sections.content:
Australia's General Skilled Migration program offers permanent residency to skilled workers with no employer sponsor required. The three points-tested pathways are Subclass 189 for independent migrants who can settle anywhere, Subclass 190 for state-nominated migrants, and Subclass 491 for regional provisional visa holders.

Alongside these, the employer-sponsored Skills in Demand visa (Subclass 482) gives Canadians a faster non-points route when a nominated role comes from an approved Australian employer. Every pathway can lead to permanent residence for the applicant and included family members.
sections.title: Skilled Migration Pathways Overview

sections.content:
The points test decides who gets invited. You need at least 65 points, though competitive rounds favour scores of 80 or more. Being 25 to 32 earns the maximum 30 points, superior English earns 20, and skilled employment adds up to 20 points across Australian and overseas experience.

Education contributes 15 to 20 points depending on qualification level. State nomination adds 5 points for Subclass 190 and 15 for Subclass 491, while partner skills, Australian study, specialist education and credentialed community language earn further points.
sections.title: The Points Test Explained

sections.content:
Before applying, obtain a positive skills assessment from the authority for your occupation, such as ACS for ICT professionals, Engineers Australia for engineers, or VETASSESS for trades. You also need competent English, shown through IELTS, PTE or an accepted equivalent, and foreign credentials assessed against Australian standards.

You then lodge an Expression of Interest through SkillSelect. If invited, you have 60 days to file the full application with health examinations, police clearances, employment references and the visa fee, which starts around 4,115 Australian dollars for the primary applicant.
sections.title: Skills Assessment and How to Apply

sections.content:
Skilled independent and nominated visas typically take six to twelve months from invitation to grant, while the Skills in Demand visa often finishes in one to three months. Complete documentation and in-demand occupations move fastest, so prepare references and clearances early.

Beyond the visa fee, budget for skills assessments, English tests, medical examinations and police clearances. Once granted, permanent residents access Medicare, and employers contribute superannuation toward retirement on top of salary.
